t: Maximum Number of Integers to Choose From a Range II — Greedy + Binary Search
o: Pick distinct integers from [1, n], avoiding banned values, maximizing the count subject to sum ≤ maxSum (up to 1e15, n up to 1e9). Clearly the optimal strategy takes the smallest allowed integers first. Example 1: allowed {2,3,5}, take 2 then 3 would exceed? sum 2+3=5 > 4, so only one integer (3 alone also works, count 1). Example 2: take 1,2,7 → count 3. Because n is huge, a linear scan may iterate ~sqrt(2*maxSum) ≈ 4.5e7 times — borderline — so the intended solution binary-searches the count and computes the sum of the x smallest allowed numbers in O(log) time using prefix sums over the sorted banned list.
k: Optimal selection is always the x smallest allowed integers — monotone in x, enabling binary search on the answer.
Sum of first x allowed integers = x(x+1)/2 minus the banned values below the x-th allowed value; the x-th allowed value is found by adjusting x upward by the number of banned values it skips.

a.i: Iterate i = 1..n, skipping banned values, accumulating until the sum would exceed maxSum. Simple and clearly correct; iteration count is bounded by roughly sqrt(2*maxSum) plus banned hits, which passes but is not asymptotically clean given n up to 1e9.
s: Put banned values into a hash set.
Scan i from 1 upward; skip banned, otherwise add i if it keeps sum ≤ maxSum.
Stop when adding would exceed maxSum; return the count.
a.t: O(sqrt(maxSum) + |banned|) — the scan stops once the triangular sum exceeds maxSum

a.n: Approach 2: Binary search on the count with prefix sums
a.i: For a candidate count x, the chosen numbers are the x smallest allowed values. If v is the x-th allowed value, their sum is v(v+1)/2 minus the banned values ≤ v. Finding v: start v = x and repeatedly set v = x + (number of banned ≤ v) until fixed — at most |banned|+1 iterations. Feasibility of x requires v ≤ n and sum ≤ maxSum. Feasibility is monotone, so binary search the largest feasible x.
s: Sort banned and build prefix sums.
Define ok(x): resolve v = x-th allowed value by fixed-point iteration with bisect counts; require v ≤ n and triangular sum minus banned prefix ≤ maxSum.
Binary search x in [0, n] for the largest feasible value.
a.t: O(|banned| log |banned| + log n · |banned|) — sorting plus binary search where each feasibility check does a small fixed-point loop over banned counts

w: Lead with the greedy observation, then present binary search for full marks on the large-n constraints. Pitfalls: forgetting the v ≤ n check (example 2 with x = 4 wants value 8 > 7), 64-bit arithmetic for sums up to ~1e15, and duplicates in banned (harmless for counting prefixes). Follow-up: maximize the number of chosen integers if each could be reused twice.
